subject: KiteFlow: sudden surge 5xx/429s — customer update & mitigation plan
body:
From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@kiteflow.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@kiteflow.com
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: sudden spike: 5xx/429s from Redwood API impacting batch ingest

Hi Vanessa —

We started seeing a pronounced uptick in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood API around 08:50 PST this morning. Our batch ingest jobs are timing out and clients are retrying aggressively; overall throughput is down ~40% compared to last week. Attached a short sample of error responses and timestamps.

Can you confirm whether this is a known degradation on your side and what the ETA is for a resolution? We’re on a tight release window and need an interim mitigation if the root cause will take time.

Thanks,
Alex Greene
Head of Platform — KiteFlow

Attachment: kiteflow_error_samples.log (text, 12 KB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@kiteflow.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, ops@kiteflow.com
Date: 2026-08-09T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike: 5xx/429s from Redwood API impacting batch ingest

Alex — thanks for flagging and for the samples. I’ve looped in SRE and the on-call manager. We’re treating this as a high-severity event. Initial ask: can you tell us if KiteFlow has changed any client-side retry timeouts or concurrency knobs in the last 24 hours? That information will help with throttling strategy.

Immediate plan (short):
- SRE will run targeted traces to identify whether 429s are originating from our gateway or downstream inference nodes.
- We’ll prepare a customer-facing note with ETA and recommended client-side backoff guidance.
- If needed, we can temporarily rate-limit KiteFlow traffic at the edge to protect overall capacity.

I’ll provide an update within 30 minutes.

-Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: RE: sudden spike: 5xx/429s from Redwood API impacting batch ingest

Team — quick triage:
- Traces show a sharp increase in queue times on inference pools serving KiteFlow’s model variant. Error breakdown last 30m: 62% 429 (gateway rate limit), 28% 5xx (worker OOM/restarts), 10% timeouts.
- KV cache eviction rates spiked after a series of large-batched requests from KiteFlow around 08:48. Their client-side retry loop is concurrent (no jitter) and is amplifying load — effectively a retry storm.
- Autoscaler saw sustained CPU/GPU pressure but didn’t scale fast enough due to conservative cooldowns for that pool (config delta from last deploy).

Immediate mitigations we can apply (ordered):
1) Enable short-term per-customer edge throttling for KiteFlow (limit to current baseline + 20%) — fast and reversible.
2) Flip to model-fallback path: route to a compatible smaller quantized variant for non-critical requests (reduces memory and latency).
3) Adjust autoscaler cooldown and do a temporary forced scale-up for the affected pool.
4) Insert a short-lived circuit breaker that returns 429 with Retry-After when queue depth exceeds threshold to prevent cascading OOMs.

I’ll push a Runbook (mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf) to the thread and start executing 1) and 3) now. ETA for visible improvement: 20–30 minutes; full recovery dependent on scale-up stabilization (~45–60 minutes).

-Neha (SRE)

Attachment: mitigation_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 320 KB)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@kiteflow.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Customer update: mitigation steps & status page sync

Alex — thanks for your patience. Quick customer-facing summary we plan to publish to you and to our status page:

-- Redwood engineers have identified a client-triggered retry amplification pattern that overwhelmed a subset of inference nodes serving KiteFlow. We are applying targeted throttling at the edge, forcing a temporary model fallback for low-priority requests, and initiating a controlled scale-up of the affected pool. We expect a noticeable reduction in errors within 30 minutes; full stabilization may take up to 60 minutes. --

Action items for KiteFlow: please apply exponential backoff with jitter for retry loops, and if possible pause large batch replays until we confirm stabilization.

I’ve drafted a status page update (statuspage_update_draft.txt) and will publish the incident page once we confirm the immediate throttle is in place and showing metrics improvement. I’ll also coordinate with Marissa on any billing/credit asks.

-Sean Gallagher
Sr. Manager, Incident Response

Attachment: statuspage_update_draft.txt (text, 3 KB)
From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@kiteflow.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jun Park <jun.park@kiteflow.com>, ops@kiteflow.com
Date: 2026-08-09T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer update: mitigation steps & status page sync

Appreciate the quick response. We’ll throttle back batch replays and add jittered backoff on our side immediately. Two asks: 1) can Redwood confirm when the throttling is lifted and whether you’ll post a timeline for rollback? 2) KiteFlow will likely request an incident credit for the window of degraded throughput — who should we engage on that?

If you can share a short timeline and an owner for credit discussions, that helps us plan the release.

— Alex

Date: 2026-08-10T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Customer update: mitigation steps & status page sync

Alex — quick follow-up and owners:
- Throttling window: applied 09:45 PST on Aug 9; we monitored and began rollback at 10:30 PST once error rate dropped below 2% for 15 minutes. Full rollback completed at 10:55 PST after autoscaler completed the forced scale-down safely. We will post a post-incident summary to the status page and include an exact timeline.
- Incident credit/compensation: Marissa Cole (cc’d) is the owner for billing/credit requests — she’ll reach out with next steps for a review and any adjustments.

We’re preparing a post-incident summary with root cause analysis, actions taken, and long-term mitigations (autoscaler tuning, adding per-customer circuit-breaker defaults, and client SDK guidance for backoff). ETA for the postmortem doc: EOD Aug 12.

Thanks for working with us on the fast rollback. Please keep this thread open for the billing conversation; Marissa will follow up.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
